title: Self-planning calendar launch — now-line intro, pile-up hook, AI prompt, 3D replan, feature close-ups, tessellation end

source.author: @lexnlin
source.note: Remade from scratch in HyperFrames after the tessel launch video; structure and pacing follow it. The brand, logo, copy, people and events are fictional placeholders — replace them before publishing.

scenes: the frame is one red dot; it shrinks, draws the now-line, and a calendar grid grows out of it
meetings fly in and pile up; the hook headline blurs in, then everything collapses into the dot
dark lockup: two blocks and the now-dot assemble into the mark, wordmark and tagline slide out
the top block opens into the app window; the week fills with events and the clash badge counts them
camera pushes onto the prompt bar; the prompt is typed with live-highlighted chips; the send button floods the screen
the red collapses into a tilted now-line; the week reshuffles in 3D, protected blocks drop in, clashes count down to none
three split-screen close-ups: a meeting slides to a free slot, a morning block refuses an invite, an overrun pushes the afternoon down
the week becomes one tile among hundreds; the field tilts, blurs, and the dot lands as the period of the end line
the end line turns into blocks that fold into the mark; lockup with domain; everything shrinks back to the dot
notes: Square brackets in the prompt mark the phrases that turn into chips once typed. Feature captions take | as a line break. The week itself (titles, times, clashes, what moves where) lives in the EV array: each row has a messy slot, a planned slot (or null when it moves to next week) and a style (g gray, h personal/hatched, k protected, o task). The result line should agree with that array: the defaults (20 moved, 14 to next week, 12 clashes) are counted from it. Clash outlines stay red regardless of the accent colour.
